summary:
Earth Jukebox: Press Play on the Planet

What if we could explore our planet not only by looking at data, but also by listening to it and interacting with it?

Earth Jukebox is an interactive platform that brings NASA’s official Earth data, visualizations, and videos together in one place. It uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and AI agents to find and organize relevant information from NASA sources, helping users explore changes happening across our planet.

Users can discover scientific information in different ways: explore interactive maps and 2D and 3D graphs, read AI-assisted explanations, create diagrams and videos, and generate research reports. They can also turn Earth data into sound, listen to audio descriptions, and download data as CSV files. WAVER SI supports the sound-generation feature.

Accessibility is an important part of our idea. By combining sound, descriptions, and interactive visuals, we want to make Earth science easier to understand and more accessible, including for people who are blind or have low vision.

Earth Jukebox brings data and different ways of experiencing science together. Our goal is simple: help more people discover the story of our changing planet.
details:
Earth Jukebox is an AI-powered application designed to help people explore and understand our changing planet using real scientific data from official NASA websites and databases.

The system connects NASA data sources with AI technologies to retrieve, organize, and present relevant scientific information in an accessible and interactive way. Rather than simply displaying raw data, it allows users to explore information through different formats, including interactive maps, visualizations, 2D and 3D graphs, AI-assisted explanations, diagrams, videos, and automatically generated research reports.

One of its main features is transforming scientific data into sound, allowing users to listen to patterns and changes in our planet. The application also provides audio descriptions and CSV data exports. WAVER SI is used to support sound generation.
